newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Appliance will not quantify loss.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Appliance will not quantify loss.

text.p: Appliance Recycling Centers of America Inc chief financial officer Kent McCoy said the company had expected a loss in the fourth quarter of about $700,000, or $0.15 per share, but he declined to quantify what the company now says will be a "substantially larger" loss for the period.
In 1995's fourth quarter, Appliance Recycling took a one-time impaired asset charge that contributed to a loss of $1 million, or $0.25 per share, on revenues of $4 million.
Without the charge, the quarterly loss a year ago was about $200,000, or $0.05 per share.
Founded in 1976 and public since 1991, Minneapolis-based Appliance Recycling is the largest U.S. recycler of major household appliances.

Its major customers until recently were electric utilities which bought recycled appliances under energy conservation programs that now face uncertain futures with deregulation of the utility industry, McCoy said.
"We've seen that market really stop," he said.
As a result, he said, "In the middle of last year, we changed our focus to open up retail stores."
The company has not made a profit since 1994, he said.
Whether the utility purchasing market returns is uncertain. "We're hopeful that will come back, but we don't see any set time-frame on it," McCoy said.
Shares in Appliance Recycling were off 1/4 to 1-3/4.

The company said Thursday it will close three recycling centers and 12 Encore retail stores. Write-offs and expenses associated with the closings will contribute to the larger-than-expected fourth-quarter loss, the company said.
Four recycling centers and 14 stores in the Midwest, all of which are profitable, will be kept, the company said.
"This gives us a chance to return to profitability next year, McCoy said.
